# Journey run: six stage gates through the pmos runtime

This file fills no template. It is generated by `tools/journey_record.py`, which drives the `pmos` command line through all six question banks the same way `tests/test_pmos_cli.py` does, on a fictional product called checkout. Every answer, name, date and proof file is FICTIONAL TEST DATA: it proves the runtime executes and enforces the loop, not anything about a real product, sponsor or reviewer. See the [examples index](README.md).

**Generated by:** `python3 tools/journey_record.py` · **Verified by:** `python3 tools/journey_record.py --check`

## What the runtime enforced

Each line below was attempted against this run and refused. The status and the
runtime's own message are reproduced, so deleting the code that enforces any one of
them changes this file and fails `python3 tools/journey_record.py --check`.

| Attempted | Outcome | What the runtime said |
|---|---|---|
| gate a bank with unanswered questions | blocked | all questions must be accepted before gate proof |
| gate a later bank, skipping the current one | blocked | only the current completed bank may be gated |
| prove a gate with no actor_id in the proof | blocked | gate proof schema mismatch: actor_id |
| approve as an actor outside the bank's pinned approvers | blocked | gate actor is not authorized by the pinned question bank; its approvers are: local-reviewer |

- when a proof's source file changes after approval the gate goes stale and nothing later completes until it is proved again, which the Staleness table below shows happening.
